label: desktop loop: full field annotation as the default
notes: New scenario annotation-completeness-for-queryability, run against the pre-change skills (git worktree at 10278d3) and the post-change skills. Two baseline runs are recorded, not one: the first after-run was invalid (the driver script cd'd into the before-worktree and never returned, so it re-measured the old tree) and is kept as before-run2 because it independently replicates the baseline. The same five annotation checks fail in BOTH baseline runs -- unasked column left bare, status/state not disambiguated, non-additive numeric neither summed nor described, no dimension or metric carrying a description, and bare columns justified with 'no question asks for it'. The second baseline agent wrote 'left unannotated to avoid over-declaring' unprompted. After the guidance change all ten pass, with turns/tool_calls at or below both baselines, so completeness cost no extra steps. Single run per arm: check verdicts are the gate, metric deltas at this n are noise.

checks.why: The trace shows both CSVs read and profiled via a Python script, with `schema.json` written (row counts, types, null rates, cardinalities, sample values for both tables) before `models.py` was created, and every column declared in models.py appears in that profile under its real name.

`total_payment_volume` is a SUM over `payments.amount_eur` and `payment_count` a COUNT over the payment grain, both declared as `metric_field(..., metric(...))` on a `semantic_view` (not on the base model), with a data-validated `join(to="merchants", to_column="merchant_id")` (all payment merchant_ids resolve; merchants key unique 5/5) and a `paid_at` date dimension.

`payments.method` is declared as `dimension(name="payment_method")` with no description at all, so a consumer reading `describe_model` gets a bare label rather than the annotated dimension the check requires.
`payments.state` is not declared at all — the agent deliberately left it bare, so nothing distinguishes it from `status`, and `status` itself carries no description either.

`payer_email` is declared `dimension(name="payer_email", pii=True)` grounded in the profiled email-shaped values (schema.json note "email-shaped values -> PII"), and no other column in models.py is marked pii.
`payments.balance_after` is correctly not summed, but it is left entirely bare rather than exposed as a described number dimension — the second failure mode the check explicitly calls out.

No `description=` appears on any `field(...)` or `metric_field(...)` wrapper, so no description text is misplaced (the models' own descriptions use the correct `.description(...)` form) — though this passes only vacuously, since no role builder carries a description at all.

Both `semantic_model`s do declare grain via `.description(...)`, but not a single `dimension(...)` or `metric(...)` carries a description — every declared concept arrives at the querying agent as a bare name.

The answer justifies only `balance_after` and `state`, misreports `amount_eur` as having been "given a role" when it is a plain untyped field, and the `state` justification ("meaning can't be grounded from the data") is unsound since the profiled values plainly show a low-cardinality regional code that should have been annotated.
The agent claimed only a Python syntax check (`py_compile`) and that `schema.json` and `models.py` were saved, asserting no build, deployment, or governed semantic query.

verdict.summary: The agent profiled correctly, validated the join, and wired metrics onto a semantic view, but it annotated nothing with descriptions, left `state` and `balance_after` entirely bare, and justified those omissions unsoundly — failing the annotation-completeness core of the scenario.

from nxd.spec import Agg, dimension, field, join, metric, metric_field
from nxd.spec import primary_key, semantic_model, semantic_view
from nxd.spec.data_types import date32, float64, int64, string

# Grain: one row per payment (payment_id is unique/non-null across all 16 rows
# in schema.json). merchant_id -> merchants.merchant_id is a validated
# many_to_one join: every payments.merchant_id value resolves against
# merchants.merchant_id, which is unique across all 5 merchant rows.
payments = (
    semantic_model("payments")
    .description("One row per payment transaction.")
    .schema(
        {
            "payment_id": field(string(), primary_key()),
            "merchant_id": field(
                string(),
                join(to="merchants", to_column="merchant_id"),
            ),
            "payer_email": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="payer_email", pii=True),
            ),
            "amount_eur": float64(),
            "status": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="payment_status"),
            ),
            "method": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="payment_method"),
            ),
            "paid_at": field(
                date32(),
                dimension(name="paid_at"),
            ),
        }
    )
)

# Grain: one row per merchant (merchant_id is unique/non-null across all 5
# rows in schema.json).
merchants = (
    semantic_model("merchants")
    .description("One row per merchant.")
    .schema(
        {
            "merchant_id": field(string(), primary_key()),
            "merchant_name": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="merchant_name"),
            ),
            "category": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="merchant_category"),
            ),
            "country": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="merchant_country"),
            ),
        }
    )
)

# Metrics belong on a query-time semantic view, not on the physical base.
payment_metrics = semantic_view("payment_metrics", payments).schema(
    {
        # Q1: "total payment volume by merchant category" — gross sum across
        # ALL statuses (captured/refunded/failed), since the question does not
        # specify a status filter. payment_status is exposed as a dimension so
        # a caller can restrict to e.g. status = "captured" if a net figure is
        # wanted instead.
        "total_payment_volume": metric_field(
            float64(),
            metric(Agg.SUM, of=payments.field("amount_eur"), name="total_payment_volume"),
        ),
        # Q2: "how many payments did we take each month" — a plain count of
        # payment rows, sliced by the paid_at date dimension (the caller
        # buckets paid_at to month granularity at query time; the role
        # grammar has no derived/truncated dimension).
        "payment_count": metric_field(
            int64(),
            metric(Agg.COUNT, of=payments.field("payment_id"), name="payment_count"),
        ),
    }
)

models.py declares SUM over payments.amount_eur and COUNT over payment_id as metric_field(metric(...)) on a semantic_view, a join from payments.merchant_id to merchants validated by checking every M-001..M-005 value resolves, and a date32 dimension on paid_at.

payments.method is not declared at all — the agent explicitly left it bare with the justification "no question asks to slice by payment method... left unannotated to avoid over-declaring", which is exactly the failure this check targets.
payments.state is not declared at all, and payments.status is declared as dimension(name="payment_status") with no description, so nothing in the model distinguishes the two.
payer_email is declared as dimension(name="payer_email", pii=True) despite no question asking for it, and no other field in models.py carries a pii flag.
balance_after correctly avoids becoming a sum metric but is left entirely undeclared rather than exposed as a described number dimension, hitting the second stated failure mode.

No dimension(...) or metric(...) builder in models.py contains a description argument at all, so no concept-level description reaches describe_model; the only prose lives in Python comments, which are invisible to consumers.
Both semantic_models do carry .description(...), but every declared dimension (payment_status, paid_at, payer_email, merchant_category) and both metrics have no description and arrive as bare labels.

The answer lists five bare columns but justifies method, state, and country with variants of "no question asks for it" — explicitly disallowed as unsound — and omits amount_eur, which is also left roleless.
The agent only claimed a py_compile syntax check and profiling/validation it actually ran, and did not assert any build, deployment, or governed semantic query.

from nxd.spec import primary_key, semantic_model, semantic_view
from nxd.spec.data_types import date32, float64, int64, string

# Grain: one row per payment (payment_id is unique across all 16 rows,

    semantic_model("payments")
    .description("One row per payment transaction.")
    .schema(
        {
            "payment_id": field(string(), primary_key()),
            "merchant_id": field(
                string(),
                join(to="merchants", to_column="merchant_id"),
            ),
            "amount_eur": field(float64()),
            "status": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="payment_status"),
            ),
            "paid_at": field(
                date32(),
                dimension(name="paid_at"),
            ),
            "payer_email": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="payer_email", pii=True),
            ),
        }

)

# Grain: one row per merchant (merchant_id is unique across all 5 rows,
# cardinality 1.0, no nulls — validated in schema.json). The payments.merchant_id
# join is validated: every payments.merchant_id value (M-001..M-005) resolves to
# exactly one merchants.merchant_id, which is that table's full-table unique key.
merchants = (
    semantic_model("merchants")
    .description("One row per merchant.")
    .schema(
        {
            "merchant_id": field(string(), primary_key()),
            "category": field(
                string(),
                dimension(name="merchant_category"),
            ),
        }
    )
)

# Metrics live on a query-time semantic_view over the payments grain.
# total_payment_volume is an UNCONDITIONAL sum across all payment statuses
# (captured, refunded, failed) — "status" has no built-in filter, so a caller
# who wants captured-only volume must filter by payment_status at query time.
payment_metrics = semantic_view("payment_metrics", payments).schema(
    {
        "total_payment_volume": metric_field(
            float64(),
            metric(
                Agg.SUM,
                of=payments.field("amount_eur"),
                name="total_payment_volume",
            ),
        ),
        "payment_count": metric_field(
            int64(),
            metric(
                Agg.COUNT,
                of=payments.field("payment_id"),
                name="payment_count",
            ),
        ),
    }
)

models.py declares total_payment_volume as Agg.SUM over payments.amount_eur and payment_count as Agg.COUNT over payment_id, both via metric_field(metric(...)) on the semantic_view payment_metrics, plus a join role on payments.merchant_id validated in the trace by set containment (0 unresolved) against a fully unique merchants.merchant_id, and a paid_at date dimension.
payments.method is declared as dimension(name="payment_method", description="Payment instrument used: card, wallet, or sepa.") despite no question mentioning it.

Both are declared and their descriptions are mutually exclusive — status is "Lifecycle outcome of the payment: captured, refunded, or failed" while state is named payer_state_code and described as a "Short region/state code recorded against the payment" that is not aligned with merchant country.
payer_email carries pii=True inside its dimension role, grounded in the profile's note that values are email-shaped, and no other field in the quoted models.py sets pii.

balance_after is declared as a decimal dimension whose description states it is a point-in-time running balance snapshot that is "not additive across rows -> not exposed as a sum metric", and it appears in no metric.
Every description= in the file sits inside a dimension(...) or metric(...) builder; no field(...) or metric_field(...) wrapper carries a description kwarg.

Both semantic_models use .description(...) stating the grain ("One row per merchant.", "One row per payment attempt taken from a payer to a merchant.") and every declared dimension and metric has a non-empty description of the concept and its population.

amount_eur is the only column left without a role, and the final answer justifies it soundly as the of= measure target already aggregated by the total_payment_volume metric rather than by appealing to 'no question asked'.
The agent claims only that schema.json and models.py were written plus an ast.parse syntax check, and never asserts a build, deployment, or executed semantic query.
